title: Integrate footprint
tagline: Design a sidecut from its radius: draw the radius along the ski as sketch lines, get the outline -- exact arcs where the radius is constant, placed so the waist lands where you ask.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: A sidecut is designed by its radii, but drawn as an outline. Integrate footprint turns a radius profile into the outline: curvature integrated twice, with the waist location (or taper) and width you set. Constant-radius stretches come out as true arcs that report their radius.
useWhen: Start a sidecut from radius targets
Try a reverse-radius flank or a transition
Need arcs that show 'R 14000' when clicked
slides.caption: IF3: profile lines at R14 m and R3 m (reverse) -> three exact, tangent arcs.

points.head: Contacts and RSL
points.body: FCP / ACP where the ski meets the snow; RSL between them, MRS its middle.

points.head: Waist, widest, inflection
points.body: Narrowest point; widest point of each half; where the curvature changes sign.

points.head: Taper
points.body: Angle of the line joining the widest points; positive when the tip is wider.

points.head: Constant radius -> arc
points.body: Closed form sin(phi) = sin(phi0) + (x - x0) / R: an exact circle, emitted as a sketch arc.

points.head: Changing radius -> spline
points.body: A sloped profile line is integrated numerically and joins the arcs tangentially.

points.head: Placed by a solver
points.body: Tangent angle solved so the waist lands at the waist location (or the taper matches), then shifted to the waist width.

slides.title: The dialog
params: APPROX / FIT: how transition splines are made.
One curve per same-sign region, or per profile edge.
One curve for all (ignored when there are arcs).
Force arcs / lines -- rational curves that do NOT report a radius.
WAIST: place the narrowest point; TAPER: set the overall taper angle.
World X of the waist (65 mm).
Full width at the waist (95 mm).
The profile sketch lines: 10 mm of y = 1 m of radius; below y = 0 = reverse.
FCP sets which end is the forebody (taper sign). ACP is not used yet.
Samples per profile edge; group output into one wire.

slides.title: Example: IF3
slides.head: Profile: R14 m core line (y = 140), R3 m reverse flanks (y = -30); waist width 200 at x = 0
slides.body: Three exact arcs R3000 / R14000 / R3000, tangent at the joints; widest points exactly at x = +-667.857. Also tested: IF1 one line -> one arc R14000; IF2 25 / 14 / 25 m -> three arcs; IF5 placed by taper 0.25 deg; IF6 sloped transitions -> exact core + 2 tangent splines.

keys: One +Y side wire: sketch arcs for constant radius, splines for transitions.
messages: No messages; a solver that does not converge stops on its last try silently.

items.head: Horizontal lines for arcs
items.body: Only a constant-radius (horizontal) profile line gives an exact arc.

items.head: Profile edges
items.body: An edge may not cross y = 0: split concave and reverse regions.

items.head: Strict
items.body: Its arcs are rational splines and report no radius; leave it off for radius callouts.
